youtube.aciklama: Modern hearing aids may treat a steady pure tone as noise and suppress it, so measurement needs a speech-like signal. ISTS was built from six women reading The North Wind and the Sun in six languages, cut into syllable-length pieces and shuffled; it is unintelligible but keeps the rhythm of speech.

cumleler: Why use speech that means nothing in any language for measurement?
Hearing aids react to incoming sound with noise reduction and compression.
A steady pure tone may be mistaken for noise and suppressed.
ISTS was built from six women speaking six different languages.
Each read The North Wind and the Sun, then recordings were shuffled.
The result is unintelligible yet speech-like, and language independent.
